data.name: Samsoniel
data.gender_notes: Samsoniel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Samsoniel is a name of Hebrew origin, derived from the Hebrew words shammas,one who guides) and el (God). In the Bible, Samson was a Nazarite who was granted superhuman strength by God, which he used to avenge his people against their enemies. Despite his strength and devotion to God, Samson was also known for his weakness for women and ultimately fell into the hands of his enemies.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of deep devotion and faith, symbolizing a strong connection to God and a commitment to living a life of service and protection.
data.etymology: Samsoniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samsoniel total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

The name can serve as a reminder of the importance of staying true to one's faith and resisting temptation, while also embodying the power and courage associated with the name Samson.
data.spiritual_significance: Samsoniel is a powerful name with deep spiritual significance. Whether used as a given name or as a source of inspiration, Samsoniel serves as a reminder of the power of faith and the importance of staying true to one's spiritual beliefs.

historical_references.reference: The name Samsoniel is believed to be derived from the biblical character Samson, who lived during the period of the Jewish judges around 1100 BC. Samson was a strong and powerful man, renowned for his strength and for his long hair, which was a symbol of his Nazarite vow.

In later European history, the name Samsoniel gained popularity during the Middle Ages. It is believed to have been a variant of the name Samuel, which was a common name during this period. The addition of the 'iel' suffix may have been inspired by the biblical names of God, such as Elias (Elijah) or Samael.

On social media platforms, individuals might use Samsoniel as their username or handle to represent their personal heritage or religious background. On genealogical sites, researchers might come across the name in old records or family trees, providing valuable historical context for those tracing their lineage.
